headline: High: social-auto-upload can exfiltrate content while risingwave provides no write or network path to constrain misuse, creating compliance and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between risingwave and social-auto-upload. risingwave has no io_surfaces or write path, and social-auto-upload uses CLI/headless tooling without a bridge to ingest risingwave outputs by default. The pairwise injection pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF an orchestrator copies risingwave output into social-auto-upload prompts or files, injection risk becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, reassess for prompt injection.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected; do not pipe outputs between them.
Disable any copy-paste or file handoff automation.
Review orchestrator wiring for shared queues or shared prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: risingwave is documented with network_egress none, while social-auto-upload has broad network egress and touches account data plus media files. There is no shared workspace or filesystem documented, so leakage is not shown by default, but if risingwave outputs are manually transferred into social-auto-upload, content could leave the local boundary.
conditions: IF risingwave outputs are copied into social-auto-upload inputs, those contents may be uploaded to third-party platforms.
IF a shared workspace is configured later, reassess for file leakage.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive data in files consumed by social-auto-upload.
Use separate directories for each agent.
Turn off any automatic upload step during testing.
Check which files social-auto-upload reads before running.
requires-engineering: add explicit allowlists for upload targets.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: risingwave has no documented write_filesystem, modify_git_state, or network egress, and social-auto-upload explicitly lacks write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and execute_shell. With no overlapping mutable resource writes documented, a capability conflict pathway is not supported.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted write access to the same directory, reassess for conflict.
IF git or database mutation capabilities are added to both agents, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible.
Do not grant shared write access to the same repo or workspace.
Run them under separate OS users.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: social-auto-upload can act on media/account data and broad network egress, so if it consumes risingwave output as authoritative content, downstream posting errors can propagate. risingwave is a data-engineering system with no documented verification handoff, so the interaction is inferred rather than directly evidenced; uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF risingwave output is fed directly into social-auto-upload without validation, cascading errors can reach published posts.
IF social-auto-upload is configured to auto-post from generated content, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before upload.
Validate schemas and filenames before passing data onward.
Use a staging account for dry runs.
Log rejected inputs for inspection.
requires-engineering: add content verification gates before posting.

E_compliance.rationale: social-auto-upload touches account data and media and has broad network egress, which can create residency or retention issues when paired with risingwave-generated content. risingwave itself has no data classes touched documented, so the compliance concern is driven mainly by social-auto-upload; the pair still creates a plausible policy mismatch if regulated content is routed through it.
conditions: IF regulated or personal content is routed through social-auto-upload, retention and residency policies must be checked.
IF account data is stored in a jurisdiction with stricter rules, reassess compliance.
mitigations: Confirm what data social-auto-upload stores.
Avoid sending regulated data through the uploader.
Use test accounts for validation.
Review retention settings before deployment.
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and residency controls.
